data.name: FGF21
data.description: Fibroblast growth factor 21, a metabolic hormone that activates AMPK/mTOR signaling to regulate glucose metabolism and wound healing.
data.description_beginner: A hormone released mostly by the liver that helps regulate blood sugar and metabolism. It works partly by activating the AMPK/mTOR signaling chain, and has also been shown to help wounds heal.

studies.title: FGF21-modified adipose stem cell-derived exosomes promote wound healing by activating fibroblast glycolysis through AMPK/mTOR signaling.
studies.authors: Chen K; Chen X; Wen C; Chen W; Liao Z; et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: FGF21-enriched exosomes from engineered ADSCs promote chronic wound healing by activating fibroblast glycolysis, with AMPK activated and mTOR signaling suppressed, improving proliferation, migration, and tissue repair in a mouse model.
